partners.mechanism_chain: Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory Protein (HGNC:11260) —DISRUPTS→ Cholesterol transport to mitochondria; Cholesterol transport to mitochondria —DECREASES→ Steroidogenesis; Steroidogenesis —LEADS_TO→ Congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia (MONDO:0008725); Ferredoxin Reductase (HGNC:3124) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0009060); Mitochondrial respiration (GO:0009060) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 9b (MONDO:0971174). Loss-of-function mutations in STAR disrupt cholesterol transport to mitochondria, severely impairing steroidogenesis and causing congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in FDXR, a key component of the mitochondrial electron transport chain, disrupt mitochondrial respiration, leading to MMD9B. Both pathways converge on mitochondrial function, with steroidogenesis specifically requiring mitochondrial activity for key enzymatic steps, and MMD9B directly impacting the core machinery of mitochondrial respiration.

falsification.text: If genetic analysis reveals that the causal variants for congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia due to STAR deficiency are exclusively associated with impaired cholesterol transport and steroidogenesis, and do not impact mitochondrial respiration, while variants causing MMD9B are solely linked to mitochondrial respiratory chain defects without affecting steroidogenesis, this hypothesis would be falsified. Specifically, if specific genetic variants in STAR are found to be pathogenic for adrenal hyperplasia but have no discernible effect on mitochondrial respiration, or if FDXR variants causing MMD9B do not indirectly compromise steroidogenic pathways, the proposed overlap mechanism would be weakened.
